title: Classifying Discontinuities of Rational and Step Functions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Classify the discontinuities of f(x) = 1/(x - 3) at x = 3 and g(x) = floor(x) at integer values x = n.
finalAnswer: f \text{ has an infinite discontinuity at } x = 3; \quad g \text{ has jump discontinuities at all } x \in \mathbb{Z}

steps.title: Analyze f(x) = 1/(x - 3) near x = 3
steps.explanation: The denominator approaches 0 through positive values from the right and negative from the left.
steps.why: Infinite limit signifies a vertical asymptote, hence an infinite discontinuity.

steps.title: Analyze g(x) = floor(x) near integer n
steps.mathExpression: \lim_{x \to n^+} \lfloor x \rfloor = n, \quad \lim_{x \to n^-} \lfloor x \rfloor = n - 1
steps.explanation: Both one-sided limits are finite but differ by 1.
steps.why: When left and right limits are finite and unequal, the discontinuity is a jump discontinuity.
